result.note: Tests the proposed SAEIA's composition and stop-gap role, the 2006 EIA framework, and the role of State EIA Authorities.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the Union government proposed a Standing Authority on Environment Impact Assessment (SAEIA). Consider the following statements:
items: The SAEIA would consist of ex-officio members appointed by the central government.
The SAEIA would permanently replace the State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities.
The Environmental Impact Assessment framework under which approvals operate was introduced in 2006.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The SAEIA would only temporarily take over the responsibilities of state-level appraisal authorities when they become inactive, for example when terms expire and new members are not appointed. The aim is to stop projects piling up in a clearance backlog.
questions.source: When state-level environmental appraisal authorities become inactive, the standing authority would temporarily take over their responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Under India's Environmental Impact Assessment framework, as described in March 2026, which bodies handle most regional projects?
options: Benches of the National Green Tribunal
Regional offices of the Central Pollution Control Board
questions.explain: Large national projects are reviewed by the central government, while most regional projects go to the State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities. The proposed SAEIA is meant to act as a backup when these state authorities stop functioning.
questions.source: Large national projects are reviewed by the central government under the EIA framework, while most regional projects are handled by the State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities locally.
